title: Animated chart with one takeaway (16:9)
description: A 12-second 16:9 data story: the title and what is measured rise in, three to six labelled values grow from zero as columns (bars when labels are long) or draw as a line, the key value keeps the accent while the rest recede, and a takeaway rises in over the source line. Code-rendered (scene.chart-story) with a lo-fi bed, a riser under the growth, a click on the focus and a swell under the takeaway.

label_1.description: Name of the first value in the brief's list, copied exactly (in 'Bus 34%, Car 28%' the first label is 'Bus'); a category or a period such as 2024

value_1.description: The first value in the brief's list as a plain number (in 'Bus 34%, Car 28%' the first value is 34; 4,200 is 4200)

label_2.description: Name of the second value in the brief's list, copied exactly (in 'Bus 34%, Car 28%' the first label is 'Bus'); a category or a period such as 2024

value_2.description: The second value in the brief's list as a plain number (in 'Bus 34%, Car 28%' the first value is 34; 4,200 is 4200)

label_3.description: Name of the third value in the brief's list, copied exactly (in 'Bus 34%, Car 28%' the first label is 'Bus'); a category or a period such as 2024

value_3.description: The third value in the brief's list as a plain number (in 'Bus 34%, Car 28%' the first value is 34; 4,200 is 4200)

label_4.description: Name of the fourth value in the brief's list, copied exactly (in 'Bus 34%, Car 28%' the first label is 'Bus'); a category or a period such as 2024; leave out when the brief lists fewer values

value_4.description: The fourth value in the brief's list as a plain number (in 'Bus 34%, Car 28%' the first value is 34; 4,200 is 4200); leave out with its label when the brief lists fewer values

label_5.description: Name of the fifth value in the brief's list, copied exactly (in 'Bus 34%, Car 28%' the first label is 'Bus'); a category or a period such as 2024; leave out when the brief lists fewer values

value_5.description: The fifth value in the brief's list as a plain number (in 'Bus 34%, Car 28%' the first value is 34; 4,200 is 4200); leave out with its label when the brief lists fewer values

label_6.description: Name of the sixth value in the brief's list, copied exactly (in 'Bus 34%, Car 28%' the first label is 'Bus'); a category or a period such as 2024; leave out when the brief lists fewer values

value_6.description: The sixth value in the brief's list as a plain number (in 'Bus 34%, Car 28%' the first value is 34; 4,200 is 4200); leave out with its label when the brief lists fewer values

title.description: Headline that states the chart's one point in plain words; no number the brief does not give

measure.description: What is measured, copied from the brief (e.g. 'share of commuters in 2025'); shown under the title

unit.description: Unit written after the values in the brief: %, GW, M (million), bn, km; empty for none

prefix.description: Currency sign written before the values in the brief ($, £, €); empty for none

highlight.description: Which value the takeaway is about: its position (1-6) in the order given, or 0 for the largest

takeaway.description: The one sentence the viewer should remember, drawn only from the brief's values; no new numbers

source.description: Who published the data, copied from the brief (e.g. 'Energy Institute, 2025'); shown as 'Source: ...'

chart.description: auto: columns (or bars when labels are long) for categories; line for one measure over time (years, months)

look.description: Visual look: night (near-black, mint), paper (cream, vermilion), ocean (deep blue, cyan), signal (black, acid lime), citrus (warm white, amber)

scene.description: The chart animation; rendered from the data unless supplied

music.description: Music bed; produced procedurally unless a cleared track is supplied

riser.description: Riser under the growth, peaking as the last mark lands

focus_hit.description: Soft click as the other marks recede and the key mark lights

copy_examples.brief: Explainer chart for a cycling charity: bike trips per day across the city's new bridges in 2025, from the council's traffic counters. Harbour Bridge 4,200, Mill Bridge 2,750, Station Bridge 1,900, Park Bridge 860. Point: the Harbour Bridge carries the most bikes. Source: City Council traffic counters, 2025.

inputs.title: Harbour Bridge carries the most bikes
inputs.takeaway: Harbour Bridge carries more bikes than any other crossing

copy_examples.note: Labels and values are copied in the brief's order and the unused slots are left out. The title states the point, the takeaway repeats it in a full sentence without adding a number, and the source is copied.

style.typography: Inter ExtraBold title, SemiBold labels, direct value labels

direction.action: Title, the marks grow from zero, the key mark is singled out, then the takeaway

notes: The animation is code (recipes/scene/chart-story) rendered frame-exactly on a virtual clock; the content model writes the title and takeaway and copies labels, values, unit, measure and source from the brief.

Labels, values, unit, prefix, measure and source are VERBATIM. Values 4-6 are optional: an unused slot keeps its defaults (empty label, value -1) and is dropped; a label without a value, or a value without a label, fails the render instead of drawing a made-up bar.
Bars and columns always start at zero, every mark is labelled directly with its value, and negative values are refused.
Beats at 12 s (independent of the number of values): growth 1.00-3.88 s under the riser, focus click at 5.40 s, takeaway swell at 6.10 s.

quality_gates.description: Integrated loudness lands within 1 LU of the -16 LUFS delivery target.
Decoded true peak stays at or below -0.5 dBTP after AAC encoding.
No stretch of blank picture (no visible contrast, any colour) lasts longer than 0.5 seconds.
A reviewer checks every label and value against the cited source, and that the highlighted value is the one the takeaway describes.
A subject-matter reviewer confirms the title and takeaway follow from the data and do not overstate it.
